summary.one_liner: A tiny, educational JavaScript interpreter written in JavaScript that interprets a small subset of the language to explain closures.
summary.what_it_does: The repository implements a small interpreter for a tiny subset of JavaScript, written in JavaScript, with the stated goal of explaining closures. The supported syntax includes numeric, boolean, null and undefined literals, identifiers, binary operators (+, -, *, /, equality and comparison forms) and unary operators (! and -). It also supports the ternary conditional, arrow function expressions (with expression or block bodies), call expressions, and const-only variable declarations. The README says there is no assignment or mutation, and const bindings behave like letrec, so recursive definitions such as a factorial example work. The README notes it is a work in progress and points to the unit tests as a place to explore. It is built for readability rather than spec compliance or speed.
use_cases: learn how closures work by reading an interpreter
study how a small language interpreter is structured
experiment with evaluating a subset of JavaScript
reference for writing a toy language in JavaScript
teaching material on interpreters and scope
notable: Explains closures by building an interpreter for them

Includes arrow functions and ternaries but no traditional function syntax
